title: TRACE: Trajectory-Aware Comprehensive Evaluation for Deep Research Agents

key_points.claim: Outcome-only metrics like Pass@1 create a misleading 'high-score illusion' for deep research agents, ignoring process quality, efficiency and soundness.
key_points.evidence_quote: a reliance on singular metrics like Pass@1, creating a "high-score illusion" that ignores the quality, efficiency, and soundness of the reasoning process

key_points.claim: Static benchmarks fail to measure robustness and latent capability.
key_points.evidence_quote: the failure of static benchmarks to quantify crucial attributes like robustness and latent capability

key_points.claim: TRACE evaluates the whole trajectory with a Hierarchical Trajectory Utility Function covering efficiency, cognitive quality (including evidence grounding), and accuracy.
key_points.evidence_quote: a Hierarchical Trajectory Utility Function that quantifies process efficiency and cognitive quality, including evidence grounding, alongside accuracy

key_points.claim: A Scaffolded Capability Assessment measures latent ability as the minimum guidance needed for success.
key_points.evidence_quote: quantifying an agent's latent ability by determining the minimum guidance needed for success

key_points.claim: Accompanying DeepResearch-Bench has controllable complexity; experiments show multi-dimensional ranking reveals accuracy/efficiency/robustness trade-offs missed by single metrics.
key_points.evidence_quote: uncovers critical trade-offs between agent accuracy, efficiency, and robustness entirely missed by singular metrics

reliability_notes: Only the abstract page was read, not the full paper, so there are no experimental numbers. It is a preprint from Feb 2026 and may not be peer reviewed. The authors propose the framework themselves, so the claims are self-reported.
